text.p: Sterling is poised to consolidate against the mark and dollar in Europe, with support around 3.0330 marks and $1.6280 holding, said technical analysts.
Chartists said sterling, which pushed to highs of 3.0455 marks and $1.6430 in late Europe on Friday, would be taking a breather on Monday before attempting to make new gains.

"We had a pretty good session on Friday. For sterling/mark we are looking for a little bit of a pullback but 3.0360 down to 3.0330 will be good support," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.
At 0735 GMT, sterling was trading at 3.0361/71 marks.
This compared with 3.0455/65 in late Europe on Friday. Against the dollar, sterling was trading at $1.6290/00 compared with $1.6330/40 in late Europe.
In the event of a stumble through support at 3.0330 marks, Celaya said the round number at 3.0 marks will hold.
"If we can hold on above this area, we could see sterling/mark attempt a push above 3.04-3.0450 marks," said Celaya.
But, he said, a slip through the 3.03 level would put sterling/mark in slippery territory with losses towards 3.01 marks seen likely.
For a volatile sterling/mark, which sank to lows of 2.9735 last week, a vault higher could be capped around 3.0455 marks, the highs visited on August 1.

For cable, which sank to $1.603 and its lowest in more than seven weeks on Wednesday, support around $1.6280 should hold. A push below a long-term trendline, dating from March 1996 and cutting in around $1.6250, would turn it shaky.

"Support should come in around $1.6280. Below there we've got $1.62 -- a big area to watch," said Celaya adding that cable is favoured to remain flat with an eventual push to $1.65 likely this week. --Julia Meehan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6701
